# Phillips

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039)</sub>
- **Role:** school teacher  <sub>[v1 c17 P37](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0037), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013)</sub>; master  <sub>[v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Phillips had tears in his eyes when he gave his farewell speech to his pupils.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)_

## Personality

Mr. Phillips is a horrid and sarcastic teacher who lacks proper control over his classroom. He frequently resorts to whipping his students yet maintains no order. He is prone to spasmodic fits of reform and exhibits a solemn, self-important attitude when delivering reprimands. However, he can show a romantic side, such as giving flowers to Prissy Andrews and writing verses.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P68](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0068), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## History

Mr. Phillips served as the school teacher at Avonlea. During his time at the school, he regularly whipped his students, including Sam Boulter, though he failed to maintain order. He spent significant time courting his student Prissy Andrews under the guise of helping her with her lessons and Queen's preparation. He publicly embarrassed Anne Shirley on her first day for poor spelling, punished her by standing her on the platform, and later made her sit next to Gilbert Blythe when she arrived late. At a local concert, he delivered a heart-stirring recitation of Mark Antony's oration. Upon his departure from the Avonlea school, he gave an affecting farewell speech that brought many of his students to tears.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P57](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0057), [v1 c15 P59](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0059), [v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_
